  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5

library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mackova_2026_fluconazole"))
cat("* Citation: ", mod$reference, "\n\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description: ", mod$description, "\n\n", sep = "")
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics18080929> (Pharmaceutics
  2026;18(8):929, open access, PMC13516392)
* Supplement: a three-page PDF with Supplementary Figures S1 (eGFR-creatinine vs
  eGFR-cystatin C against individual clearance), S2 (goodness-of-fit) and S3
  (visual predictive check). It carries no parameter value that is absent from the
  main text.

Mackova and colleagues fitted a one-compartment model with linear elimination to
183 routine therapeutic-drug-monitoring serum concentrations from 116 hospitalised
adults treated with intravenous fluconazole. Creatinine-based CKD-EPI 2021 eGFR,
entered as a time-varying regressor, scales clearance; adjusted body weight scales
the volume of distribution. The paper then simulates three standard regimens
against an eGFR-based maintenance-dose nomogram with a loading dose.

# Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
pop <- mod$population
cat(sprintf("* Species: %s\n", pop$species))
cat(sprintf("* Subjects / observations: %d patients, %d serum concentrations\n",
            pop$n_subjects, pop$n_observations))
cat(sprintf("* Age: median %s, range %s\n", pop$age_median, pop$age_range))
cat(sprintf("* Total body weight: median %s, range %s; adjusted body weight %s\n",
            pop$weight_median, pop$weight_range, pop$adjusted_weight))
cat(sprintf("* Female: %.1f%%\n", pop$sex_female_pct))
cat(sprintf("* Disease: %s\n", pop$disease_state))
cat(sprintf("* Renal function: %s\n", pop$renal_function))
cat(sprintf("* Dosing: %s\n", pop$dose_range))
cat(sprintf("* Region: %s\n", pop$regions))
```

Baseline demographics are in Mackova 2026 Table 1 (Results 3.1).

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: one compartment, linear elimination, IV infusion | -- | Results 3.2, first paragraph |
| `lvc` (Vd at ABW 75 kg) | 41.58 L | Table 2, Vd_pop |
| `lcl` (CL at eGFR 90 mL/min) | 0.81 L/h | Table 2, CL_pop |
| `e_abw_vc`, Vd = Vd_pop x (ABW/75)^beta | 2.28 | Table 2, beta_Vd_ABW and the equation row above it |
| `le_crcl_cl`, CL = CL_pop x (eGFR/90)^beta | log(0.43) | Table 2, beta_CL_eGFR and the equation row above it |
| `etalvc` | 0.44^2 | Table 2, BSV Vd = 0.44 |
| `etalcl` | 0.25^2 | Table 2, BSV CL = 0.25 |
| `etale_crcl_cl` | 1.24^2 | Table 2, BSV beta_CL_eGFR = 1.24 |
| `propSd` | 0.18 | Table 2, Error model, Proportional |
| ABW = IBW + 0.4 (TBW - IBW), Devine IBW | -- | Methods 2.2 |
| eGFR: CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine, time-varying regressor | -- | Methods 2.2, 2.3; Results 3.2 |
| Typical Vd 41.58 L, CL 0.81 L/h, t1/2 35.6 h | -- | Results 3.2 (checked below) |
| Nomogram MD = 769.5 (eGFR/90)^0.43 mg/day | -- | Results 3.3; Figure 3 |
| Loading dose 2.8 x MD; day-10 / day-1 AUC24 887.66 / 318.09 | -- | Results 3.3 |
| Probability of target attainment | -- | Table 3 |
| Steady-state AUC24 = 24.35 Cmin + 51.51 | -- | Figure 1 |

# Structural parameters and the typical patient

```{r params}
th <- setNames(mod$iniDf$est, mod$iniDf$name)
typ <- c(
  vc   = unname(exp(th["lvc"])),
  cl   = unname(exp(th["lcl"])),
  thalf = unname(log(2) * exp(th["lvc"]) / exp(th["lcl"]))
)
round(typ, 2)

# Deterministic: the packaged values reproduce the typical patient quoted in
# Results 3.2 (Vd 41.58 L, CL 0.81 L/h, t1/2 35.6 h) to the paper's rounding.
stopifnot(
  abs(typ[["vc"]] - 41.58) < 0.005,
  abs(typ[["cl"]] - 0.81) < 0.005,
  abs(typ[["thalf"]] - 35.6) < 0.05
)
```

Typical clearance and volume across the covariate ranges in Table 1:

```{r covariate-ladder}
tibble(
  `eGFR (mL/min)` = c(10, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150),
  `Typical CL (L/h)` = round(typ[["cl"]] * (`eGFR (mL/min)` / 90)^0.43, 3)
) |> knitr::kable()

tibble(
  `ABW (kg)` = c(45, 60, 75, 90, 110),
  `Typical Vd (L)` = round(typ[["vc"]] * (`ABW (kg)` / 75)^th[["e_abw_vc"]], 1)
) |> knitr::kable()
```

## Typical-value steady state (PKNCA)

A typical patient (eGFR 90 mL/min, ABW 75 kg) receiving 200 mg every 24 h as a 1-h
infusion for 20 days must reach `AUC0-24 = dose / CL = 246.9 mg*h/L`.

```{r typical-ss, warning = FALSE}
ev_typ <- rxode2::et(amt = 200, dur = 1, ii = 24, addl = 19, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 480, by = 0.25), cmt = "central") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(id = 1L, CRCL = 90, ABW = 75, treatment = "200 mg q24h typical")

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_typ,
                           keep = "treatment", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame()

conc_typ <- sim_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(id = 1L) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_typ <- ev_typ |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment) |>
  mutate(duration = 1)

nca_typ <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_typ, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_typ, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular",
                   duration = "duration"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 456, end = 480, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE,
                         cmin = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
typ_res <- as.data.frame(nca_typ$result) |>
  select(PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
typ_res

auc_ss <- typ_res$PPORRES[typ_res$PPTESTCD == "auclast"]
thalf_nca <- typ_res$PPORRES[typ_res$PPTESTCD == "half.life"]
# Deterministic solve against its own closed form. Residual is the 0.25-h
# linear-up/log-down trapezoid on the 1-h infusion ramp plus <0.1% of residual
# accumulation after 20 days (13.5 half-lives); both well under 0.5%.
stopifnot(
  abs(auc_ss / (200 / 0.81) - 1) < 0.005,
  abs(thalf_nca / 35.6 - 1) < 0.01
)
```

# The dosing nomogram (Figure 3)

The maintenance dose equation of Results 3.3, `MD = 769.5 x (eGFR/90)^0.43`, is
exactly `AUC24 x CL_pop x (eGFR/90)^0.43` with an AUC24 target of
769.5 / 0.81 = 950 mg*h/L, the value printed in the Figure 3 title.

```{r nomogram, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Mackova 2026: once-daily fluconazole maintenance dose as a function of eGFR."}
nomogram_dose <- function(egfr) 769.5 * (egfr / 90)^0.43
ld_factor <- 2.8

nomo <- tibble(eGFR = seq(10, 150, by = 1), dose = nomogram_dose(eGFR))
ggplot(nomo, aes(eGFR, dose)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1200), breaks = seq(0, 1200, 200)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(10, 150, 10)) +
  labs(x = "eGFR (mL/min)", y = "Dose (mg)",
       title = "Target: steady-state AUC24 of 950 mg*h/L") +
  theme_bw()

# Implied AUC target, from the model's own typical clearance.
auc_target <- 769.5 / typ[["cl"]]
# Curve end-points read off Figure 3 by the maintainers (about 300 mg at
# eGFR 10 and about 960 mg at eGFR 150). Deterministic arithmetic, so the
# slack is only the read-off precision.
stopifnot(
  abs(auc_target - 950) < 1,
  abs(nomogram_dose(10) / 300 - 1) < 0.03,
  abs(nomogram_dose(150) / 960 - 1) < 0.03
)
```

# Virtual cohort

The original TDM records are not public, and the paper's Monte Carlo simulations
resampled its own 116 patients 500 times. This vignette instead draws a 200-subject
virtual cohort whose eGFR and adjusted-body-weight marginals reproduce Table 1
exactly at the minimum, quartiles and maximum: each covariate is drawn by pushing a
uniform variate through a monotone spline of the five reported quantiles. eGFR and
ABW are drawn independently because the paper reports no correlation between them,
and eGFR is held constant over each subject's 10 days.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20260808)
n_sub <- 200L

draw_from_quantiles <- function(n, q) {
  stats::splinefun(c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), q, method = "hyman")(stats::runif(n))
}

cohort <- tibble(
  id   = seq_len(n_sub),
  CRCL = draw_from_quantiles(n_sub, c(8, 55, 86, 103, 160)),
  ABW  = draw_from_quantiles(n_sub, c(43, 68, 75, 84, 110))
)

cohort |>
  summarise(across(c(CRCL, ABW),
                   list(min = min, q1 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.25), median = median,
                        q3 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.75), max = max))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything()) |>
  mutate(value = round(value, 1))
```

# Simulation of the dosing strategies (Figure 2)

Six arms are solved on the same cohort, each with 1-h infusions over 10 days:

* A: 400 mg loading dose, then 200 mg every 24 h (cryptococcosis label regimen)
* B: 800 mg loading dose, then 400 mg every 24 h (invasive candidiasis label regimen)
* C: 400 mg every 12 h (off-label high dose)
* D: eGFR nomogram maintenance dose every 24 h after a 2.8-fold loading dose
* D0: the nomogram maintenance dose without the loading dose, from which the paper
  derived the 2.8 multiplier
* F1: 200 mg every 24 h without a loading dose, the regimen behind Figure 1

The random-number generator is reseeded before each solve, so every arm shares the
same between-subject random effects (common random numbers) and cross-arm
comparisons are paired.

```{r arms}
inf_dur <- 1
obs_times <- seq(0, 240, by = 1)

make_arm_events <- function(label, dose_times, md_vec, ld_vec) {
  dosing <- cohort |>
    mutate(md = md_vec, ld = ld_vec) |>
    crossing(time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(amt = if_else(time == 0, ld, md), evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
           rate = amt / inf_dur)
  obs <- cohort |>
    crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", rate = NA_real_)
  bind_rows(dosing, obs) |>
    mutate(arm = label) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, rate, CRCL, ABW, arm) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

q24 <- seq(0, 216, by = 24)
q12 <- seq(0, 228, by = 12)
md_nomo <- nomogram_dose(cohort$CRCL)
const <- function(x) rep(x, n_sub)

arm_events <- list(
  make_arm_events("A: LD 400 + 200 mg q24h", q24, const(200), const(400)),
  make_arm_events("B: LD 800 + 400 mg q24h", q24, const(400), const(800)),
  make_arm_events("C: 400 mg q12h",          q12, const(400), const(400)),
  make_arm_events("D: LD + MD nomogram",     q24, md_nomo, ld_factor * md_nomo),
  make_arm_events("D0: MD nomogram, no LD",  q24, md_nomo, md_nomo),
  make_arm_events("F1: 200 mg q24h, no LD",  q24, const(200), const(200))
)
stopifnot(vapply(arm_events,
                 function(e) !anyDuplicated(e[, c("id", "time", "evid")]),
                 logical(1)))
```

```{r solve-arms}
solve_arm <- function(ev, seed = 20260808L) {
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(seed)
  set.seed(seed)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, keep = "arm") |>
    as.data.frame()
}
sim <- bind_rows(lapply(arm_events, solve_arm))

# Common-random-numbers guard: one clearance per subject across all six arms.
stopifnot(
  nrow(distinct(sim, id, cl = signif(cl, 8))) == n_sub,
  all(sim$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim$Cc, na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

```{r figure-2, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Mackova 2026: simulated fluconazole serum concentrations. Line = median; bands = 5th-27.5th, 27.5th-50th, 50th-72.5th and 72.5th-95th percentiles of the 200-subject virtual cohort."}
fig2 <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), substr(arm, 1, 2) %in% c("A:", "B:", "C:", "D:")) |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), q275 = quantile(Cc, 0.275),
            q50 = median(Cc), q725 = quantile(Cc, 0.725),
            q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(fig2, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q275, ymax = q725), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = q50)) +
  facet_wrap(~arm, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 240, 48)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (mg/L)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The day-10 median peak (1 h after the last dose) and trough (240 h) are compared with
values the maintainers read off the median lines of Figure 2.

```{r figure-2-compare}
fig2_read <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                       ~what,    ~pub,
  "A: LD 400 + 200 mg q24h",  "peak",   13.7,
  "A: LD 400 + 200 mg q24h",  "trough",  8.2,
  "B: LD 800 + 400 mg q24h",  "peak",   27.3,
  "B: LD 800 + 400 mg q24h",  "trough", 16.5,
  "C: 400 mg q12h",           "peak",   47.5,
  "C: 400 mg q12h",           "trough", 37.0,
  "D: LD + MD nomogram",      "peak",   49.0,
  "D: LD + MD nomogram",      "trough", 29.5
)
peak_time <- c("A:" = 217, "B:" = 217, "C:" = 229, "D:" = 217)
fig2_sim <- fig2 |>
  mutate(key = substr(arm, 1, 2)) |>
  filter(time == 240 | time == peak_time[key]) |>
  transmute(arm, what = if_else(time == 240, "trough", "peak"), sim = q50)

fig2_cmp <- left_join(fig2_read, fig2_sim, by = c("arm", "what")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim / pub - 1))
fig2_cmp |>
  mutate(across(c(sim, pct_diff), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  rename(Arm = arm, `Day-10 point` = what, `Figure 2 median (mg/L)` = pub,
         `Simulated median (mg/L)` = sim, `% difference` = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(nrow(fig2_cmp) == 8, !anyNA(fig2_cmp$sim))
```

```{r figure-2-assert}
# A mis-transcribed Vd, CL or exponent moves every median by tens of percent.
# The tolerance admits the read-off precision and the different covariate
# distribution of a 200-subject virtual cohort versus the authors' 116 real
# patients (whose eGFR also varied over time). Achieved: median 2.4%,
# max 4.4% (regimen D peak).
stopifnot(
  abs(median(fig2_cmp$pct_diff)) < 10,
  max(abs(fig2_cmp$pct_diff)) < 25
)
```

# PKNCA: day-1 and day-10 exposure

```{r cohort-nca, warning = FALSE}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= 24 | time >= 216) |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, arm)

dose_df <- bind_rows(arm_events) |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, arm) |>
  mutate(duration = inf_dur)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h"),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id, doseu = "mg",
                   route = "intravascular", duration = "duration"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = c(0, 216), end = c(24, 240),
                         auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
))

nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "cmin")) |>
  mutate(day = if_else(start == 0, "day1", "day10")) |>
  select(arm, id, day, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(PPTESTCD, day), values_from = PPORRES)

stopifnot(nrow(nca_tbl) == n_sub * length(arm_events), !anyNA(nca_tbl$auclast_day10))

nca_tbl |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(`AUC0-24 day 1` = median(auclast_day1),
            `AUC216-240 day 10` = median(auclast_day10),
            `Cmax day 10` = median(cmax_day10),
            `Cmin day 10` = median(cmin_day10)) |>
  mutate(across(-arm, \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  rename(Arm = arm) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated NCA parameters (mg*h/L, mg/L).")
```

## Probability of target attainment (Table 3)

Efficacy is `AUC24 / MIC >= 100` (AUC24 >= 200 mg*h/L at MIC 2 mg/L, >= 400 at
MIC 4 mg/L); toxicity is AUC24 > 1500 mg*h/L, all on day 10.

```{r table3}
published_t3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                       ~pta_mic2, ~pta_mic4, ~pta_tox,
  "A: LD 400 + 200 mg q24h",  75.86,     13.79,     0.86,
  "B: LD 800 + 400 mg q24h",  98.28,     75.86,     4.31,
  "C: 400 mg q12h",           99.14,     98.28,     14.66,
  "D: LD + MD nomogram",      100.00,    97.41,     8.62
)

t3_sim <- nca_tbl |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(sim_mic2 = 100 * mean(auclast_day10 >= 200),
            sim_mic4 = 100 * mean(auclast_day10 >= 400),
            sim_tox  = 100 * mean(auclast_day10 > 1500), .groups = "drop")

t3 <- inner_join(published_t3, t3_sim, by = "arm")
stopifnot(nrow(t3) == 4)

t3 |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  rename(Regimen = arm,
         `Published MIC 2 (%)` = pta_mic2, `Simulated MIC 2 (%)` = sim_mic2,
         `Published MIC 4 (%)` = pta_mic4, `Simulated MIC 4 (%)` = sim_mic4,
         `Published AUC24 > 1500 (%)` = pta_tox, `Simulated AUC24 > 1500 (%)` = sim_tox) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PTA on day 10: Mackova 2026 Table 3 vs the virtual cohort.")
```

```{r table3-assert}
eff_diff <- c(t3$sim_mic2 - t3$pta_mic2, t3$sim_mic4 - t3$pta_mic4)
tox_diff <- t3$sim_tox - t3$pta_tox
# Eight efficacy PTAs: achieved max 3.2 points, median 0.4. One binomial SE at
# 200 subjects is at most 3.5 points (p = 0.5), so 15 points is >4 SE. A
# mis-transcribed CL, Vd or eGFR exponent moves the PTAs of arms A and B by
# tens of points. Toxicity PTAs: achieved max 0.9 points; SE at p = 0.15 is
# 2.5 points, so 8 points is >3 SE. These bounds are a transcription check:
# the alternative readings of the random effects (additive exponent IIV, or
# Table 2 BSV read as a variance) shift the PTAs by only 7-10 points, which a
# 200-subject cohort cannot reliably resolve.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(eff_diff)) < 15, abs(median(eff_diff)) < 6,
  max(abs(tox_diff)) < 8
)
```

All twelve probabilities agree with Table 3 to within the Monte Carlo error of a
200-subject cohort, including the toxicity column, which depends on the far tail
of the clearance distribution and therefore on both the size and the log-normal
form of the random effect on the eGFR exponent.

## Loading-dose multiplier

The paper derives the 2.8-fold loading dose from the median AUC24 on day 10
(887.66 mg*h/L) divided by that on day 1 (318.09 mg*h/L) under the nomogram
maintenance dose (Results 3.3), here arm D0.

```{r loading-dose}
d0 <- nca_tbl |> filter(arm == "D0: MD nomogram, no LD")
ld_cmp <- tibble(
  quantity = c("Median AUC24 day 1", "Median AUC24 day 10", "Ratio of medians"),
  published = c(318.09, 887.66, 887.66 / 318.09),
  simulated = c(median(d0$auclast_day1), median(d0$auclast_day10),
                median(d0$auclast_day10) / median(d0$auclast_day1))
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / published - 1))
ld_cmp |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  rename(Quantity = quantity, Published = published, Simulated = simulated,
         `% difference` = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable()

# Day-1 AUC24 depends on Vd and the dose only, so it pins the volume model;
# the ratio pins the elimination rate. Tolerances admit the virtual-cohort
# difference; a mis-transcribed Vd or ABW exponent moves both by >20%.
# Achieved: day 1 -0.3%, day 10 +4.8%, ratio +5.1%.
stopifnot(all(abs(ld_cmp$pct_diff) < 15))
```

## Trough-exposure relationship (Figure 1)

Figure 1 regresses the steady-state (day 10) AUC24 on Cmin after 200 mg every 24 h
without a loading dose: `AUC24 = 24.35 x Cmin + 51.51`.

```{r figure-1, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1 of Mackova 2026: day-10 AUC24 versus trough concentration after 200 mg every 24 h (1-h infusion). Dashed line: the published regression."}
f1 <- nca_tbl |> filter(arm == "F1: 200 mg q24h, no LD")
fit <- stats::lm(auclast_day10 ~ cmin_day10, data = f1)
coef(fit)

ggplot(f1, aes(cmin_day10, auclast_day10)) +
  geom_point(shape = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "black") +
  geom_abline(intercept = 51.51, slope = 24.35, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "Cmin (mg/L)", y = "AUC24 (mg*h/L)") +
  theme_bw()

# The slope is set by the elimination rate; a wrong Vd or CL moves it by
# tens of percent. Achieved slope 24.7 (+1.4%), intercept 58.4.
stopifnot(abs(coef(fit)[["cmin_day10"]] / 24.35 - 1) < 0.15)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Random effect on the eGFR exponent.** Table 2 reports a between-subject
  variability of 1.24 for beta_CL_eGFR. eGFR entered the Monolix model as a
  time-varying regressor (Methods 2.3), which requires its exponent to be declared
  as an individual parameter, and Methods states that all model parameters were
  log-normally distributed. The exponent is therefore encoded as
  `0.43 x exp(eta)`, eta ~ N(0, 1.24^2). The alternative additive reading,
  `0.43 + eta`, would make the exponent negative in 36% of patients (clearance
  rising as renal function falls). In a large steady-state check by the
  maintainers the additive reading gives 71% for the MIC-2 PTA of regimen A and
  the log-normal reading 78%, against the published 75.9%; the PTAs alone do not
  decide between the readings, so the paper's statement on distributions does. The same
  research group used the same construction for daptomycin
  (`Subrtova_2026_daptomycin`).
* **Between-subject variability scale.** Table 2's BSV values (0.44, 0.25, 1.24) are
  read as Monolix omega, the standard deviation of the random effect on the log
  scale, and squared for `ini()`.
* **eGFR units.** The paper labels eGFR as mL/min throughout, although CKD-EPI 2021
  returns mL/min/1.73 m^2 and the paper quotes its augmented-renal-clearance
  threshold in those units. Supply the CKD-EPI value as reported.
* **Nomogram AUC target.** Methods 2.4 states the nomogram was designed for an AUC24
  of 850 mg*h/L, but the nomogram equation (769.5 / 0.81 = 950) and the Figure 3
  title both correspond to 950 mg*h/L. This vignette follows the equation.
* **Virtual cohort.** eGFR and adjusted body weight are drawn independently from
  their Table 1 quantiles and held constant over time; the paper resampled its own
  patients, with time-varying eGFR. Only 200 subjects per arm are simulated, so the
  probabilities of target attainment carry about 3 percentage points of Monte
  Carlo error.
* **Figure 2 values** compared above were read off the published figure by the
  maintainers and carry read-off error of roughly 0.5 mg/L.
* **No erratum** to the article was found (checked 2026-11-16).
